answer.rationale: p99 latency spike of 5x target following a release 2 hours ago is a strong signal of regression in the write path. Memory_b1 shows rolling back cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact; this is the direct precedent. Memory_b2 is critical to verify because it warns that writes are currently heavy during settlement peak—failover is explicitly contraindicated in this state ('never fail over while writes are hot'), which eliminates regional_failover despite its historical success. Rollback is lower-risk than capacity provisioning (no time to validate), circuit breaker (should not mask the core issue), or read replicas (irrelevant to write path latency). However, latency climb could also indicate load rather than code; flagging downstream risk. Rolling back does preserve the option to investigate root cause post-recovery.
